summary: Claude Code treated the open-ended "build a notifications system" request as design work: it loaded the brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, explored the repo, and ran a structured multi-question design dialogue (scope → architecture → stack → subscription semantics) ending in a proposed design and a request for approval. No implementation code was written.
reasoning: All three criteria are supported by the session log and screen text: brainstorming skill first, no implementation files written, design direction produced and approval requested. Only nit is the skill namespace differing from the criterion wording, which I read as a rename rather than a failure.

observations.description: Skill id mismatch vs. the story: the log shows `Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"}`, while the acceptance criterion names `superpowers:brainstorming`. Appears to be a plugin rename; worth confirming the expected namespace.

Scope creep risk: the user asked for notifications on a 'tiny tasks page', and the agent's recommended path expands to a full FastAPI + SQLite backend, users table, event log, and three sequenced sub-projects. Defensible reasoning, but a user with a one-file index.html may find the recommendation disproportionate.

The agent asserted the toolchain is 'your documented toolchain is Python-first (micromamba/uv, ruff, mypy)' although the repo contains only index.html and a .git dir; the basis for that claim was not visible to me on screen.
Each question round took roughly 30-60s of think time with the screen mostly static; the log was the only reliable progress indicator.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'The fork: whether this project's scope is "notifications on top of an app we design and build here" or "a notifications design against an app someone else is building."' followed by forks on 'Where do tasks live?', 'Which stack for the tasks backend?', 'What makes a user "care about" a task?'. Session log tool list contains no Write/Edit: `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming / Bash ls -la && git log / Read .../index.html / AskUserQuestion x4`; workdir still only has index.html (168 bytes).

criteria.criterion: brainstorming skill invoked BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over 82bcd457-216f-4114-83cb-1c165f642fa6.jsonl lists tool calls in order, first being `Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming`; grep of the same list shows zero Write/Edit entries for the session.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Four AskUserQuestion calls with recommended options (e.g. 'My recommendation: server-backed... You described a multi-user outcome'); I accepted each recommendation and counted them as good behavior, not against the agent.
